nodes.name: Fe-alkoxide solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.10 g of Fe(NO3)2·9H2O was dispersed in 40 mL of isopropanol and 8 mL of glycerol mixed solution under stirring. Subsequently, the above mixture was transferred to 100 mL autoclave and reaction continued for 6 h at 180°C. After cooling to room temperature, the Fe-alkoxide precursor was centrifuged, washed with ethanol, and dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Fe-alkoxide precursor: 0.10 g of Fe(NO3)2⋅9H2O was dispersed in 40 mL of isopropanol and 8 mL of glycerol mixed solution under the stirring. Subsequently, the above mixture was transferred to 100 mL of autoclave and the reaction was continued for 6 h at 180°C. After cooling, the Fe-alkoxide precursor was centrifuged and washed with ethanol, and followed by drying under vacuum at 60°C for overnight.

nodes.name: P/M-FeS2 CVD sulfurization
nodes.procedure: 20 mg as-synthesized Fe-alkoxide precursor placed downstream and 700 mg sulfur powder placed upstream (4 cm distance) in tube furnace (SK-G06123K, tube 60 mm OD × 54 mm ID × 1000 mm L). Heated to 350°C at 5°C/min under 10 L/min Ar flow for 4 h to obtain P/M-FeS2 nanospheres.

nodes.characterization_summary: P/M-FeS2 exhibits spherical morphology, most particles (55%) ca. 350 nm diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FE-SEM images (Fig. 2a and Fig. S5a) reveal the P/M-FeS2 with a spherical morphology, most of which (55 %) are ca. 350 nm in diameter (Fig. S5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows P/M-FeS2 porous structure; HR-TEM reveals lattice spacings 0.27 nm ((200) P-FeS2) and 0.23 nm ((120) M-FeS2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 2b and Fig. S6a) show the P/M-FeS2 with porous structure. HR-TEM image reveals two different lattice spacings of 0.27 and 0.23 nm, corresponding to the (200) plane of P-FeS2 and (120) plane of M-FeS2 (Fig. 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: P/M-FeS2 has specific surface area of 17.14 m²/g, pore size 21.03 nm, pore volume 0.09 cm³/g; P-FeS2: 11.47 m²/g; M-FeS2: 11.76 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area, pore size and pore volume of P/M-FeS2, P-FeS2 and M-FeS2 were measured by N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms... the specific surface area of P/M-FeS2 is 17.14 m² g⁻¹, which is higher than those of P-FeS2 (11.47 m² g⁻¹) and M-FeS2 (11.76 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of P/M-FeS2 displays two sets of characteristic diffraction rings attributed to P-FeS2 and M-FeS2 structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern also displays two sets of characteristic diffraction rings, which can be attributed to the P-FeS2 and M-FeS2 structures, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDX shows uniform Fe and S distribution across P/M-FeS2 nanosphere.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular darkfield scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) together with the energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping image shows evenly distributed Fe and S elements on the entire P/M-FeS2 nanosphere (Fig. S6b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD identifies phase structures of P-FeS2 and P/M-FeS2; diffraction peaks at 33.1° and 37.1° in P/M-FeS2 show slight shift; Rietveld refinement gives M-FeS2:P-FeS2 ratio of 45.9%:54.1%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2e shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) of the products, from which the phase structures of P-FeS2 and P/M-FeS2 can be identified... the ratio between M-FeS and P-FeS2 in P/M-FeS2 determined by the XRD Rietveld refinement is 45.9%:54.1 %.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show Eg (343 cm⁻¹) and A1g (376 cm⁻¹) modes of P-FeS2; P/M-FeS2 shows A1g blue shift and additional Ag modes (324, 388 cm⁻¹) of M-FeS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2f presents Raman spectra of P-FeS2 and P/M-FeS2. The peaks at 343 and 376 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the Eg and A1g vibration models of P-FeS2, respectively... two additional peaks at 324 and 388 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the Ag vibration model of M-FeS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺; in P/M-FeS2, Fe²⁺ 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 shift higher by 0.10-0.15 eV; S 2p shows S₂²⁻ (162.4, 163.6 eV) with negative shift, polysulfides (165.1 eV), SO₄²⁻ (168.5, 169.7 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed... the high-resolution Fe 2p spectra exhibit characteristic signals of Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ orbitals... For the S 2p spectra in P/M–FeS2, the peaks at around 162.4 and 163.6 eV can be attributed to S₂²⁻ 2p3/2 and S₂²⁻ 2p1/2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES of P/M-FeS2 shifts to higher energy vs P-FeS2, indicating increased Fe oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2i, the Fe K-edge of the P/M-FeS2 is slightly shifted to a higher energy compared to P-FeS2, indicating an increased oxidation state of Fe after the introduction of M-FeS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge EXAFS shows Fe-S (1.83 Å), Fe-Fe (2.89, 3.46 Å) bonds; minimal coordination differences between P/M-FeS2 and P-FeS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed EXAFS... an obvious peak at 1.83 Å can be belonged to the Fe-S bond coordination. Besides, the peaks at around 2.89 and 3.46 Å were attributed to Fe-Fe coordination.
